programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Feumaidh an Dùd Beag a bhith far an urrainn dha bhith dùdach fad’ an là. Gu mì-fhortanach, chaidh e air seachran ach fhuair e a shlighe dhachaidh gu Planaid nan Dùd, le beagan taic bho a charaidean ùra Little Dùd needs to be where he can hoot all day. Unfortunately, he goes missing but finds his way back home to Planet Dùd, with a little help from his new friends.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air Meaban is Moo gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo, às dèidh dha cearc gheal nochdadh sa bhothan, tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan eile a tha geal a lorg. Linda visits Meaban and Moo to set them fun challenges. After a white chicken lands in the hut, she tasks them with finding three other things that are white.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Marvin, Oona and Silky are playing hide-and-seek in the Underwater Cave. Silky tries lots of different hiding places but feels frustrated when Oona and Marvin find her easily. When it's her turn to look for her friends, Silky is too slow on land and is disappointed when she can't find her friends. But when she agrees to play once more, Silky finds a hiding place that's just right for her! Tha Marvin, Oona is Silky a' cluich Falach-fead san Uamh Fo-uisg'. Tha Silky a' feuchainn tòrr dhiofair àitichean falaich, ach tha i air a ruigheachd nuair a lorgas Oona is Marvin i gun strì. Nuair a thig an t-àm dhì-se a' caraidean a lorg, tha Silky ro mhall air tìr, 's tha i tàmailteach nuair nach lorg i a caraidean. Ach le aont' cluich aon trup eile, tha Silky ri lorg àite-falaich a tha fèir ceart dhìth-se!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: It's a hot day on Puffin Rock, and Oona, May and Marvin want to swim in the pond but find the water has dried up, meaning no swimming today! Even the frogs are gone... all but one, and he's hopping away. Where is he going? The friends hop along to find out - follow the frog sounds like a fun game! The frog leads them all over the island, but will they be able to keep up with him and find his friends? Latha teth a th' ann air Creag Nam Buthaidean, 's tha Oona, May is Marvin 'son snàmh san loch, ach tha an loch air tiormachadh... 's le sin cha bhi snàmh ann an-diugh. Tha fiù 's gach losgann air teicheadh... gach fear ach aon, 's tha esan ri leum air falbh. Cà' bheil e a' dol? Tha na caraidean a' leum 'son fuasgladh fhaighinn air a' chùis... Deagh gheam' a th' ann an Lean an Losgann! An losgann gan toirt air feadh an eilein.'N tèid ac' air cumail ris an losgann, agus a charaidean a lorg?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Peicein a’ fiathachadh a charaidean gu àite-obrach athar. Ach chan eil Dadaidh Pheicein a’ leigeil leotha suathadh ann an dad ach an t-ùrlar, is tha sin a’ fàs dòrainneach. Mu dheireadh thall, tha Dadaidh Pheicein a’ sealltainn dhaibh gun urrainn saorsainneachd a bhith air leth spòrsail. Petit invites his friends to his dad's workplace. But his dad won't let them touch anything except the floor and they start to get really bored. Finally, Petit's dad shows them how carpentry can be lots of fun.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Thig còmhla ri na h-Abadas air turas spòrsail eile agus iad a' sireadh facal ùr: 'sgòth'! Tha na càirdean a' cnuasachadh air an fhacal ùr seo agus tha aon dhiubh a' sealltainn ris na speuran airson faighinn a-mach dè th'ann an sgòth. The friends ponder the word 'cloud' and one of them reaches for the sky to discover exactly what a cloud looks like and what it does.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Kim Carnie a’ leughadh Carson Nach Fhaod Mise Cluich? Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Elizabeth Hawkins agus a dhealbhachadh le Bill Bolton. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Kim Carnie reads Carson Nach Fhaod Mise Cluich? written by Elizabeth Hawkins, illustrated by Bill Bolton and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha Partaidh nam Fiaclairean dol a thachairt, the Mrs Oh 'g iarraidh buidealair. Ach chan eil Mgr P deònach taic a thoirt seachad. Dè nì Stella is an Teaghlach Rìoghail airson cuideachadh leis a’ chuirm? When the Dentist Party is about to take place, Mrs Oh would like a butler. But Mr P isn’t prepared to help out. What will Stella and the Royal Family do to help at the event?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella air a glacadh eadar Mia is Freya nuair a tha ‘ad ag argamaid. Ciamar a gheibh i fuasgladh air an trod gus am bi ‘ad air ais nan caraidean a-rithist Stella is caught between Mia and Freya when they argue. How will she find a solution to the fighting so that they will be friends again?

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Chuir Míriam eòlas air surfadh nuair a bha i sia bliadhna a dh’ aois ‘s nuair a tha i san uisge, tha a h-inntinn falamh, tha i a’ faireachdainn sèimh agus ann an sunnd math. Míriam learnt to surf at six years old and when she’s in the water, her mind goes blank, she feels calm and in a great mood.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha dùbhlan aig Sebastian nuair a tha an trèan air falbh às aonais Sonaidh, oir tha aige ri Sonaidh fhaighinn air ais oirre - gun fhiosta do mhàthair Sonaidh! Sebastian has a challenge on his hands when the train has left without Sonaidh, as he has to get him back on board without Sonaidh’s mother realising!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Timmy a' faicinn cho grannach 's a tha an tuathanach agus e cruaidh air aon de na treud tha e a' cur roimhe fhèin blasad a thoirt dha air cò ris a tha e coltach a bhith na chaora. Ach nuair a thig an uair an tuathanach tilleadh, chan eil cùisean cho sìmplidh ri sin. When Timmy sees a particularly grumpy farmer giving one of the flock a hard time, he decides to give him an idea of what it's like to be a sheep. However, things aren't quite so simple when the time comes to have the old farmer back.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Cumaidh Bircher Muesli a’ dol thu fad na maidne, agus air a stòradh sa frids, faodar a chumail airson latha no dhà! A Bircher muesli will keep you going all morning, and by being stored in the fridge it will stretch for a few days! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Mach à Seo!
programme.desc: Ramsay sails to the Isle of Eigg for a fun-filled holiday. Tha Ramsay a’ seòladh gu ruige eilean Eige son latha no dhà gun tiotan na thàmh.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: Murdina is thrown into turmoil when she realises that Johan is becoming a majority shareholder in the mill. Manager Sìleas offers newcomer Rory a job as one of the drivers. But just who exactly is this mysterious Irish stranger, Rory? Ivor and Dòmhnall’s relationship is put to the test when Ivor shares his fears that he may be responsible for the fire. Tha Murdina troimhe-chèile nuair a tha i ag ionnsachadh gur ann aig Johan a bhios an roinn as motha ‘sa mhuileann. Tha Sìleas, ceannard na muilne, a’ toirt obair do Rory mar dhraibhear, ‘s e air ùr nochdadh. Ach cò dìreach a th’ anns a’ choigreach Èireannach, Rory? Tha buaireadh eadar Ivor is Dòmhnall, le Ivor ag aideachadh gur dòcha gur esan as coireach airson an teine. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Tommy Burns
programme.desc: Deich bliadhna bho bhàsaich e le aillse ’s gun e ach leth cheud ‘sa h-aon bliadhna a dh’aois, tha clann-nighean is mic Tommy Burns a’ coimhead air ais air air a bheatha mar athair gaolach, cluicheadair ball-coise cliùiteach agus manaidsear air Celtic is Cille Mheàrnaig. Ten years on from his death from cancer at just 51 years old, Tommy Burns’s daughters and sons look back on the life and career of their beloved father, a much-revered player and manager of both Celtic and Kilmarnock.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Latha dhà aig Belladrum 2025 agus tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air an t-seinneadair blues is Americana, Elles Bailey, gu Àrd-Ùrlar a’ Ghàrraidh. Dìreach air Duaisean Blues na Rìoghachd Aonaichte 2025 a choisinn, tha dòigh-seinn Bailey is measgachadh de cheòl fhreumhan, rock is ceòl-dùthchail a’ glacadh aire sluagh Bhelladrum. It’s day two at Belladrum and Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome blues and Americana sensation Elles Bailey to the Garden Stage. Fresh off her coveted 2025 UK Blues Awards triumphs, Bailey’s smoky vocals and soulful blend of roots, rock and country captivate the Belladrum crowd.

programme.title: Ar Ceol 2024 | Scotland in Music
programme.desc: Tha Megan NicGill-Fhaolain a’ toirt thugainn cruinneachadh dhen cheòl beò as fheàrr bho na tachartasan-ciùil as motha ann an Alba ann an 2024. Le ceòl a chaidh a chlàradh gu h-àraidh aig Celtic Connections, a’ chuirm iongantach a bh’ aig Skipinnish aig Caisteal Dhùn Èidinn a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna, agus dhà dhen na tachartasan ciùil as motha dhen bhliadhna – Duaisean Na Trads agus Hoolie 2024. Megan MacLellan presents highlights from another year of amazing live music in Scotland from some of the country’s top events in 2024. Featuring bespoke recordings and gig footage from Celtic Connections, and coverage from Skipinnish’s incredible 25th anniversary show at Edinburgh Castle as well as two of the biggest traditional music events of the year - The Trad Awards and Hoolie 2024. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: ...Sings Dylan
programme.desc: A look through the archives at some of the many artists who have come into BBC studios to sing their versions of Bob Dylan songs. Featured performers include Peter, Paul and Mary, Lulu, The Byrds, Joan Baez, Eric Clapton, Madeleine Peyroux, Bryan Ferry, UB40, Julie Felix, Manfred Mann, The Brian Auger Trinity and Pops Staples.

programme.title: ...Sings Dylan II
programme.desc: A feast of cover versions of Bob Dylan songs from the BBC archives, with classic tracks old and new and some surprises from the 1960s to the present. From the essential folk queen Joan Baez to punk princess Siouxsie and the Banshees, from The Hollies to Adele, taking in the likes of Julie Felix, Richie Havens, Bryan Ferry and KT Tunstall along the way, the programme reflects Dylan's long career of writing extraordinary songs and the fascination of other artists with them. Peter, Paul and Mary's sublime The Times They Are A-Changin' rubs shoulders with the close harmony of Cliff Richard and The Nolan Sisters' smooth interpretation of the protest classic Blowin' in the Wind. The Blues Band's energetic 1980s updating of Maggie's Farm contrasts with Tom Jones's powerful rootsy What Good Am I? A treat for the Dylan fan and the Dylan novice alike.

programme.title: Bob Dylan: Shadow Kingdom
programme.desc: A showcase of Bob Dylan with his band in an intimate setting as he performs songs from his extensive body of work, including Forever Young, I'll Be Your Baby Tonight, It's All Over Now Baby Blue and many more. This film marks Bob Dylan's first concert since 2019 and the first performance since his acclaimed album Rough and Rowdy Ways.

programme.title: Tangled Up with Dylan: The Ballad of AJ Weberman
programme.desc: Documentary chronicling the life, times and crimes of Bob Dylan obsessive AJ Weberman, who spent years rooting through Dylan's rubbish to try to gain insight into his life.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Munya Chawawa found viral fame during the lockdown for his satirical videos on social media. Now he has a new Channel 4 documentary, Wrestling with Trump, which looks at the links between professional wrestling and the MAGA movement. Restrictions on prisoners in the UK speaking to journalists are in focus after the Guardian was told Jeremy Bamber can no longer exchange letters or phone calls with journalists. Bamber was convicted in 1986 of murdering his adoptive family and is serving life in prison. Simon Hattenstone, feature writer at the Guardian, and Emily Bolton, defence lawyer and founder of Objection, set out the issues. The top parenting influencers, often dubbed as “momfluencers”, can earn millions. The phenomena is the subject of a new book, Like, Follow, Subscribe: Influencer Kids and the Cost of a Childhood Online. Its author, Fortesa Latifi, and Jasmine McInnes, family and travel influencer, discuss the world of “sharenting”.

Also on the programme, the drivers left fearing for their families’ safety when expensive SUVs developed a power-steering fault.

Christina presents a show all about our furry, feathered and four-legged friends, and looks back at the teams who have sniffed out some tail-wagging treasures. Expect cuddly cats, delightful dogs and even a few perky pigs as Christina visits an RSPCA centre in Hertfordshire. She counts down the most profitable pet-related items purchased by red and blues teams at antiques fairs across the country. In Kent, a statue of a golden retriever turns the head of Jenny, who runs a doggy display team; in Carmarthenshire, a couple hope to reel in a good deal with a french-glass fish; and in Nottinghamshire, a silver metal spider brooch gives best friends Pam and Diane the creeps! Away from the shopping, Eric learns about the origin of Nipper, the iconic HMV dog, and Charlie’s off the leash, learning about antique dog collars.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of celebrity comedians, featuring Susan Calman, John Thomson, Jon Culshaw and Shazia Mirza, takes on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: If there was ever an episode for animal lovers, it’s this one! Christina presents a show all about our furry, feathered and four-legged friends, and looks back at the teams who have sniffed out some tail-wagging treasures. Expect cuddly cats, delightful dogs and even a few perky pigs as Christina visits an RSPCA centre in Hertfordshire. She counts down the most profitable pet-related items purchased by red and blues teams at antiques fairs across the country. In Kent, a statue of a golden retriever turns the head of Jenny, who runs a doggy display team; in Carmarthenshire, a couple hope to reel in a good deal with a french-glass fish; and in Nottinghamshire, a silver metal spider brooch gives best friends Pam and Diane the creeps! programme.desc: If there was ever an episode for animal lovers, it’s this one! In Kent, a statue of a golden retriever turns the head of Jenny, who runs a doggy display team; in Carmarthenshire, a couple hope to reel in a good deal with a french-glass fish; and in Nottinghamshire, a silver metal spider brooch gives best friends Pam and Diane the creeps! One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: If there was ever an episode for animal lovers, it’s this one! Christina presents a show all about our furry, feathered and four-legged friends, and looks back at the teams who have sniffed out some tail-wagging treasures. Expect cuddly cats, delightful dogs and even a few perky pigs as Christina visits an RSPCA centre in Hertfordshire. She counts down the most profitable pet-related items purchased by red and blues teams at antiques fairs across the country. In Kent, a statue of a golden retriever turns the head of Jenny, who runs a doggy display team; in Carmarthenshire, a couple hope to reel in a good deal with a french-glass fish; and in Nottinghamshire, a silver metal spider brooch gives best friends Pam and Diane the creeps! Away from the shopping, Eric learns about the origin of Nipper, the iconic HMV dog, and Charlie’s off the leash, learning about antique dog collars.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of celebrity comedians, featuring Susan Calman, John Thomson, Jon Culshaw and Shazia Mirza, takes on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

Kicking off the festival as Friday night’s Main Stage headliner is the ultimate party starter, Fatboy Slim. The man who helped take dance music from club floors to festival main stages worldwide is set to bring his legendary show to the north east for a high-energy, hands-in-the-air frenzy. With what promises to be a blockbuster set, expect crowd favourites and his trademark barefoot style - this is the ultimate Friday night Dance Party.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin come to the aid of people stuck with paying a monthly contract for expensive smartphones that were never delivered - and their phone companies don’t seem to want to help. Also on the programme, the drivers left fearing for their families’ safety when expensive SUVs developed a power-steering fault.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: It's a labour of love for two brothers who create a wonderful home for their sister in Chesterton, while Martin is puzzled by a door leading nowhere in Plymouth and Dion follows a speedy flat renovation in Wales.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: If there was ever an episode for animal lovers, it’s this one! Christina presents a show all about our furry, feathered and four-legged friends, and looks back at the teams who have sniffed out some tail-wagging treasures. Expect cuddly cats, delightful dogs and even a few perky pigs as Christina visits an RSPCA centre in Hertfordshire. She counts down the most profitable pet-related items purchased by red and blues teams at antiques fairs across the country. In Kent, a statue of a golden retriever turns the head of Jenny, who runs a doggy display team; in Carmarthenshire, a couple hope to reel in a good deal with a french-glass fish; and in Nottinghamshire, a silver metal spider brooch gives best friends Pam and Diane the creeps! Away from the shopping, Eric learns about the origin of Nipper, the iconic HMV dog, and Charlie’s off the leash, learning about antique dog collars.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: Celebrating a fantastic week at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show 2026, Nicki Chapman and Angellica Bell are joined by Dame Mary Berry to reveal which garden has won the BBC RHS People’s Choice Award. Florist to the stars Hamish Powell shows you how to create fabulous floral displays, and we answer more of your questions in the Chelsea Garden Clinic.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having met online and fallen in love just over a year ago, today's couple are calling on the help of Nicki Chapman to find them their very first home together in the East Sussex countryside. To better understand what living in this county is like, Nicki meets up with one of its residents, none other than fellow Escape to the Country presenter Alistair Appleton. Alistair welcomes Nicki to his beautiful, off-grid, 200-year-old former coastguard’s cottage, which he calls home.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team restore some Victorian stage machinery, Suzie hears a story of injustice from apartheid South Africa, and wood lover Will gets to grips with the delicate art of marquetry.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of celebrity comedians, featuring Susan Calman, John Thomson, Jon Culshaw and Shazia Mirza, takes on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop

Can the model capture the spirit of a community that endured so much?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: It's a labour of love for two brothers who create a wonderful home for their sister in Chesterton, while Martin is puzzled by a door leading nowhere in Plymouth and Dion follows a speedy flat renovation in Wales.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: If there was ever an episode for animal lovers, it’s this one! Christina presents a show all about our furry, feathered and four-legged friends, and looks back at the teams who have sniffed out some tail-wagging treasures. Expect cuddly cats, delightful dogs and even a few perky pigs as Christina visits an RSPCA centre in Hertfordshire. She counts down the most profitable pet-related items purchased by red and blues teams at antiques fairs across the country. In Kent, a statue of a golden retriever turns the head of Jenny, who runs a doggy display team; in Carmarthenshire, a couple hope to reel in a good deal with a french-glass fish; and in Nottinghamshire, a silver metal spider brooch gives best friends Pam and Diane the creeps! Away from the shopping, Eric learns about the origin of Nipper, the iconic HMV dog, and Charlie’s off the leash, learning about antique dog collars.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: Celebrating a fantastic week at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show 2026, Nicki Chapman and Angellica Bell are joined by Dame Mary Berry to reveal which garden has won the BBC RHS People’s Choice Award. Florist to the stars Hamish Powell shows you how to create fabulous floral displays, and we answer more of your questions in the Chelsea Garden Clinic.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having met online and fallen in love just over a year ago, today's couple are calling on the help of Nicki Chapman to find them their very first home together in the East Sussex countryside. To better understand what living in this county is like, Nicki meets up with one of its residents, none other than fellow Escape to the Country presenter Alistair Appleton. Alistair welcomes Nicki to his beautiful, off-grid, 200-year-old former coastguard’s cottage, which he calls home.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team restore some Victorian stage machinery, Suzie hears a story of injustice from apartheid South Africa, and wood lover Will gets to grips with the delicate art of marquetry.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of celebrity comedians, featuring Susan Calman, John Thomson, Jon Culshaw and Shazia Mirza, takes on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Sarah the Lumberjill is the fourth generation of her family to 'take up the saw', working across the forests of the Central Highlands of Scotland, where her family have worked for 150 years. After some of the worst storms to hit Scotland in a lifetime, Sarah, her dad Ralph and brother Ralphy are busier than ever - though with Ralph's health in decline, Sarah has a lot to learn before taking over one day.

programme.title: Back from the Brink
programme.desc: As we continue to expand our urban spaces and cities, our wildlife has felt the consequences. Wildlife film-maker Libby Penman showcases the incredible work of dedicated conservationists who are fighting to bring our wildlife back from the brink. As we journey across Europe, we see how bottlenose dolphins are thriving in Aberdeen Harbour, how pioneering designers in Munich are reimagining urban construction with wildlife at its heart, and we meet the Ibizan scientific community that is rallying towns together to save an iconic lizard species. We see teams in Scotland that are working to protect peregrine falcons from poachers and the citizen science project in Ireland that is researching how red foxes are adapting to our city life, and dive with a dedicated woman creating change in the waterways of the Netherlands. Across all of these stories, Libby reveals the benefits of supporting and living alongside our wildlife. The amazing work of these groups and individuals show that if we take care of nature, it will take care of us in return.

programme.title: Pitch Invasion: How the Scottish and Irish Changed Football
programme.desc: How the flair and artistry of players like George Best and Kenny Dalglish inspired the biggest football clubs in England.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: There’s a big wedding to organise, so the Craiglang pals all rally round to sort a venue, flowers, food and even a band. But will it all go without a hitch?

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 2008. After a breakdown, Niall learns that Ruben has returned. Obsession takes hold, and a charged confrontation forces the brothers to face their fractured past.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: After an emotional funeral for his dad, Colin and Cathy have the neighbours round but understandably Colin is not his usual upbeat self. Christine was not impressed with the service or the priest and, as usual, is not backward about coming forward with her opinions on the whole affair. And as Beth, Eric and Ian try to make their excuses to leave early, Cathy manages to foil their escape by inviting more of the neighbours in. As the drink flows with Cathy's encouragement, Colin reminisces about the late departed Willie and encourages his neighbours to do the same. But as the guests look on - brandy glasses in hand - Cathy tries to turn the solemn occasion into a party, complete with wildly inappropriate music and games.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Sarah the Lumberjill is the fourth generation of her family to 'take up the saw', working across the forests of the Central Highlands of Scotland, where her family have worked for 150 years. After some of the worst storms to hit Scotland in a lifetime, Sarah, her dad Ralph and brother Ralphy are busier than ever - though with Ralph's health in decline, Sarah has a lot to learn before taking over one day.

programme.title: Back from the Brink
programme.desc: As we continue to expand our urban spaces and cities, our wildlife has felt the consequences. Wildlife film-maker Libby Penman showcases the incredible work of dedicated conservationists who are fighting to bring our wildlife back from the brink. As we journey across Europe, we see how bottlenose dolphins are thriving in Aberdeen Harbour, how pioneering designers in Munich are reimagining urban construction with wildlife at its heart, and we meet the Ibizan scientific community that is rallying towns together to save an iconic lizard species. We see teams in Scotland that are working to protect peregrine falcons from poachers and the citizen science project in Ireland that is researching how red foxes are adapting to our city life, and dive with a dedicated woman creating change in the waterways of the Netherlands. Across all of these stories, Libby reveals the benefits of supporting and living alongside our wildlife. The amazing work of these groups and individuals show that if we take care of nature, it will take care of us in return.

programme.title: Pitch Invasion: How the Scottish and Irish Changed Football
programme.desc: How the flair and artistry of players like George Best and Kenny Dalglish inspired the biggest football clubs in England.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: There’s a big wedding to organise, so the Craiglang pals all rally round to sort a venue, flowers, food and even a band. But will it all go without a hitch?

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 2008. After a breakdown, Niall learns that Ruben has returned. Obsession takes hold, and a charged confrontation forces the brothers to face their fractured past.

programme.title: Two Doors Down

programme.title: Freddie Flintoff's Field of Dreams
programme.desc: Time is running out for sporting legend Freddie Flintoff to help his unlikely cricket team transform, both on and off the field. With the Indian tour reaching its final few days, attention turns to life back in England, and Freddie has his work cut out dealing with thoughts of back home and future fears. Hoping to end the tour on a high, Freddie and the boys head to one of the oldest cricket clubs in India to take on their toughest opponents yet.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Georgie’s best mate Vicky is the ultimate dating ice queen. Vicky is super-picky, has a long list of unrealistic criteria for her perfect match, dumps guys for using the wrong emojis, analyses everything they do and walks out of 60 per cent of her dates. Tired of hearing about Vicky’s first date failures and delivering advice that gets ignored, Georgie calls on sex and relationships expert Oloni for an urgent intervention. Oloni wants Vicky to see where it's all going wrong, so she dishes out some cold, hard truths as she unpacks Vicky’s dating history and shows her some frank and honest video feedback from friends, family and even exes, to prove to Vicky that her bad dating behaviour needs a serious reboot. Oloni has to pull out all the stops to melt this ice queen as she sets Vicky up on a series of first dates that will challenge her behaviour and make her a better dater. Under the watchful eye of Oloni and Georgie, is Vicky ready for a change, will she give the guys a chance, be nice and let her guard down, or will she retain her ice queen crown?

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip and Ravi find out more about Andie’s secret life, and when Pip is presented with a new piece of evidence, she reaches a crisis point and questions whether Sal is guilty.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: It’s the team’s most confounding puzzle yet when a passenger boards a flight to Dominica but then seemingly vanishes mid-flight, only to be found back on Saint Marie soil... shot dead. The pilot and flight attendant deny ever seeing the victim on their plane, raising the team’s suspicions. Two further suspects are found back in Saint Marie – it transpires the victim had been caught up in a messy love affair. Neville starts to question whether he’s losing his mind, seriously doubting himself for the first time, until all the pieces of the puzzle finally fit together, revealing the startling truth. Meanwhile, an old face has returned, and Neville has a huge decision to make.

programme.desc: Best friends Sam and James want to throw one last big party with their friend Xav before they all go their separate ways to uni. Which agent will host their last hurrah?

programme.title: Big Proud Party Agency
programme.desc: Best friends Libby and Jess from Southampton want to arrange an unforgettable 18th birthday party for identical twins Holly and Charlotte, who are Libby’s younger sisters. Despite having already turned 18, the twins never got to celebrate in the proper style due to the pandemic, so the girls are hoping the Big Proud Party Agency can put things right. After hearing what the girls have to say, the party agents compete to win the business. Ryan pitches a VIP glam-up disco with high-fashion style and paparazzi. Christopher whets the appetite with a pool party featuring some half-naked 'mermen', and Teddy wants to set sail on a superyacht before ending the night in a super club. After Libby and Jess choose their favourite party idea, it’s time to get down to business. The winning party agent, supported by the others, heads to Southampton to put their plan into action. The décor has to be hand-picked to suit the theme, performers are auditioned for their very specific talents, and a dance routine is lined up as an extra special surprise. Will the twins get the 18th birthday party they always wanted?

programme.title: Big Proud Party Agency
programme.desc: Best friends Levi and Beth from Cardiff want to organise a class prom for their musical theatre year group who graduated without the normal celebrations due to Covid restrictions. They want the event to centre around leading light Geraint, aka Queen G, who has become noticeably introverted after a homophobic attack left him fearing for his life. After getting their head around the brief, the party agents compete to win the business. Ryan tempts Levi and Beth with his High School Musical-inspired Americana prom. Teddy wants the theme of her party to draw on the 1980s underground ballroom scene - complete with male strippers, and Christopher promises a decadent art deco black and gold affair in a stunning country mansion. After Levi and Beth choose their favourite party idea, it’s time to get down to business. The winning party agent, supported by the others, heads to Cardiff to put their plan into action. A bespoke couture outfit is designed, an amazing ornamental centrepiece is crafted from scratch, and the venue’s doors need to be altered to accommodate a giant glitter ball. Will Geraint rediscover his inner Queen G?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through the islands of Sardinia and Corsica sees him leave Sardinia and arrive into Corsica, the most mountainous island in the Mediterranean. In Ajaccio, he delves into the early life of the island’s most famous son, Napoleon Bonaparte, discovering how Corsica’s unique approach to childhood shaped the future conqueror. At a bustling food market, Michael samples the island’s wild herbs. He is captivated by the haunting harmonies of polyphonic singing, a sound deeply woven into the island’s soul. He then boards the legendary Trinichellu, Corsica’s historic metre-gauge mountain railway, for a breathtaking journey through the island’s rugged interior. In the heart of the wilderness, Michael discovers how cutting-edge technology and drones are being used in the battle against devastating wildfires, a crucial innovation protecting Corsica and beyond.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: In his first interview since resigning from government, former health secretary Wes Streeting talks about what went wrong for Keir Starmer, and why he should be the man to replace him.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an Impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out and they must try again tomorrow. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single Impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge in the tenth heat of the series. The specialist subjects are the life of Anne Lister, Dear Evan Hansen, Elizabeth I and the feature films of David Lynch.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Daisy mucks in with Tippy and Gus, getting her hands dirty, while Louis, seeking advice on the value of Oakley, visits Hilary and gets more insight than he bargained for. Daisy learns about the Behind the Vines showcase from Nic, and Vic delivers some bad news to Marissa and Don. Meanwhile, Daisy and Louis hope to ease their financial woes with a visit to the bank but discover they may not be on the same page after all and that failing to comply with the 'law of the land' can have consequences. Daisy makes the ultimate sacrifice for the future of Oakley, giving the run-down vineyard a chance of survival. Or will it merely be a stay of execution?

programme.title: Wonders of Life
programme.desc: Brian Cox considers what it is about our world that makes it a home for life and asks what transformed this once barren planet into the earth we know today.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. A Welsh dresser with no drawer handles, a travelling chamber stick used in the Crimean War and a sledge flag from Shackleton's ill-fated Antarctic trip of 1916 cause great excitement for the experts in Tenby.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the ancestral home of the Spencer family, Althorp in Northamptonshire. Nineteen generations have lived here, employing local people to work at the house and vast estate. Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and Will Axon find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Christina is drawn to a 1950s toy pedal car, and Will finds a Mouseman tray. Paul Martin discovers how the Grand Union Canal was the waterway equivalent of the M1 as he takes to the water on a narrow boat and discovers what life was like for the boat people who ferried cargo from A to B.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Mediterranean railway adventure reaches its finale in Corsica as he boards one of Europe’s most dramatic railways, which winds through the island’s breathtaking landscapes. Braving the heights, he takes a close-up look at the Pont du Vecchio, a spectacular viaduct along the route. In a forest of ancient chestnut trees, Michael discovers how this humble fruit is turned into an unexpected foodstuff which has sustained Corsicans for centuries. Michael learns how a by-product from the hives of the aggressive Corsican black bee is being used to create a new wonder product. His journey culminates in the stunning mountain town of Corte, where he uncovers an astonishing piece of British history and comes face to face with the resilient spirit of the Corsican people.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin, along with guest judge and gardening fan Fred Sirieix, continue the search to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. First up is Anne’s Kilcootry Barn Gardens in Fintona, with two and a half acres of mixed gardens – filled with flower beds, a vegetable garden and an apple orchard. In Omagh, the judges visit a field of dreams – 17 acres of once-barren farmland that’s been transformed by Sir Bob and Lady Rosemary, with a formal Italianate area and a large woodland, planted with wildlife in mind. Finally, it’s off to the shores of Rossglass beach, overlooking Dundrum Bay, to visit artist Bernard’s romantic rose garden. Judges Diarmuid, Carol and Fred are searching for a garden which the owners have put their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide deserves to be the last contender for the title of Greatest Garden?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cuningham show how to help the pollinators in your garden and at Beechgrove as they focus on planting that will attract bees to your plot. Even if you don’t have a garden, Kirsty demonstrates how you can help the local ecosystem by sowing a meadow in a pot. She also discusses the best summer bulbs to plant now for fragrance and colour. Brian is back in the vegetable plot for his summer-long guide to productive gardening for beginners, and there is a demonstration of how to prune spring-flowering shrubs. All that and the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: It’s the end of the week at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show 2026, and Monty Don and Arit Anderson are celebrating the great British summer as we all get ready to spend more time in our gardens. Adam Frost has plenty of design ideas for garden structures, and Frances Tophill reveals which new variety has been named Plant of the Year.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From scandalous society portraits to glittering royal furniture and the restoration of lost landscapes, this episode reveals how the legacy of the Grand Tour continues to shape Britain’s great houses – and the work being done today to protect their remarkable stories for the future.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: At the forefront of its genre, the roll call of stand-ups who have performed in front of the famous Live At The Apollo lights plays out like a who’s who of comedic royalty, and this series is no different. Each episode will see a national (and sometimes international!) stand-up both compering and performing, before introducing two of the best established and up-coming stand-ups to the stage. This episode of Live at the Apollo is hosted by the fantastic Guz Khan as he introduces the fabulous Kiri Pritchard-McLean and the amazing Rhys James. Other acts to appear throughout the series include: Tom Allen, Rosie Jones, Kae Kurd, Sindhu Vee, Alex Edelman, Lou Sanders, Darren Harriott, Jessica Fostekew, Stephen Bailey, Desiree Burch, Paul McCaffrey, Jonny Pelham, Ardal O'Hanlon, Sara Barron, Mawaan Rizwan, Sarah Pascoe, Chris McCausland and Flo & Joan

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: And Now for Something Completely Different
programme.desc: The first film version of classic sketches and memorable moments from the Monty Python gang's long-running television series, including Nudge Nudge, Hell's Grannies, Killer Cars, Dead Parrot, Lumberjack Song, Blackmail and Upper Class Twit of the Year.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Married at First Sight UK is one of Channel 4’s biggest shows, in which complete strangers marry in a mock-wedding and cameras follow what happens next. Panorama investigates allegations that raise serious concerns that welfare procedures on the reality show have failed contributors, leaving them at risk of harm. Noor Nanji speaks to three women who allege sexual misconduct by their former on-screen husbands. Two of the women say they were sexually assaulted. The men deny all the allegations against them, and both Channel 4 and CPL - the independent production company that makes the series - say the welfare protocols are robust and comprehensive. Following this Panorama investigation, Channel 4 has announced an external review into contributor welfare and has removed all previous seasons of MAFS UK.

A Welsh dresser with no drawer handles, a travelling chamber stick used in the Crimean War and a sledge flag from Shackleton's ill-fated Antarctic trip of 1916 cause great excitement for the experts in Tenby.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the ancestral home of the Spencer family, Althorp in Northamptonshire. Nineteen generations have lived here, employing local people to work at the house and vast estate. Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and Will Axon find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Christina is drawn to a 1950s toy pedal car, and Will finds a Mouseman tray. Paul Martin discovers how the Grand Union Canal was the waterway equivalent of the M1 as he takes to the water on a narrow boat and discovers what life was like for the boat people who ferried cargo from A to B.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Mediterranean railway adventure reaches its finale in Corsica as he boards one of Europe’s most dramatic railways, which winds through the island’s breathtaking landscapes. Braving the heights, he takes a close-up look at the Pont du Vecchio, a spectacular viaduct along the route. In a forest of ancient chestnut trees, Michael discovers how this humble fruit is turned into an unexpected foodstuff which has sustained Corsicans for centuries. Michael learns how a by-product from the hives of the aggressive Corsican black bee is being used to create a new wonder product. His journey culminates in the stunning mountain town of Corte, where he uncovers an astonishing piece of British history and comes face to face with the resilient spirit of the Corsican people.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin, along with guest judge and gardening fan Fred Sirieix, continue the search to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. First up is Anne’s Kilcootry Barn Gardens in Fintona, with two and a half acres of mixed gardens – filled with flower beds, a vegetable garden and an apple orchard. In Omagh, the judges visit a field of dreams – 17 acres of once-barren farmland that’s been transformed by Sir Bob and Lady Rosemary, with a formal Italianate area and a large woodland, planted with wildlife in mind. Finally, it’s off to the shores of Rossglass beach, overlooking Dundrum Bay, to visit artist Bernard’s romantic rose garden. Judges Diarmuid, Carol and Fred are searching for a garden which the owners have put their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide deserves to be the last contender for the title of Greatest Garden?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cuningham show how to help the pollinators in your garden and at Beechgrove as they focus on planting that will attract bees to your plot. Even if you don’t have a garden, Kirsty demonstrates how you can help the local ecosystem by sowing a meadow in a pot. She also discusses the best summer bulbs to plant now for fragrance and colour. Brian is back in the vegetable plot for his summer-long guide to productive gardening for beginners, and there is a demonstration of how to prune spring-flowering shrubs. All that and the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: It’s the end of the week at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show 2026, and Monty Don and Arit Anderson are celebrating the great British summer as we all get ready to spend more time in our gardens. Adam Frost has plenty of design ideas for garden structures, and Frances Tophill reveals which new variety has been named Plant of the Year.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From scandalous society portraits to glittering royal furniture and the restoration of lost landscapes, this episode reveals how the legacy of the Grand Tour continues to shape Britain’s great houses – and the work being done today to protect their remarkable stories for the future.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: At the forefront of its genre, the roll call of stand-ups who have performed in front of the famous Live At The Apollo lights plays out like a who’s who of comedic royalty, and this series is no different. Each episode will see a national (and sometimes international!) stand-up both compering and performing, before introducing two of the best established and up-coming stand-ups to the stage. This episode of Live at the Apollo is hosted by the fantastic Guz Khan as he introduces the fabulous Kiri Pritchard-McLean and the amazing Rhys James. Other acts to appear throughout the series include: Tom Allen, Rosie Jones, Kae Kurd, Sindhu Vee, Alex Edelman, Lou Sanders, Darren Harriott, Jessica Fostekew, Stephen Bailey, Desiree Burch, Paul McCaffrey, Jonny Pelham, Ardal O'Hanlon, Sara Barron, Mawaan Rizwan, Sarah Pascoe, Chris McCausland and Flo & Joan

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: And Now for Something Completely Different
programme.desc: The first film version of classic sketches and memorable moments from the Monty Python gang's long-running television series, including Nudge Nudge, Hell's Grannies, Killer Cars, Dead Parrot, Lumberjack Song, Blackmail and Upper Class Twit of the Year.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Married at First Sight UK is one of Channel 4’s biggest shows, in which complete strangers marry in a mock-wedding and cameras follow what happens next. Panorama investigates allegations that raise serious concerns that welfare procedures on the reality show have failed contributors, leaving them at risk of harm. Noor Nanji speaks to three women who allege sexual misconduct by their former on-screen husbands. Two of the women say they were sexually assaulted. The men deny all the allegations against them, and both Channel 4 and CPL - the independent production company that makes the series - say the welfare protocols are robust and comprehensive. Following this Panorama investigation, Channel 4 has announced an external review into contributor welfare and has removed all previous seasons of MAFS UK.

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: Matty and Leanne are pulled in different directions, and Gary's money laundering unravels at a tense casino night.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through the islands of Sardinia and Corsica sees him leave Sardinia and arrive into Corsica, the most mountainous island in the Mediterranean. In Ajaccio, he delves into the early life of the island’s most famous son, Napoleon Bonaparte, discovering how Corsica’s unique approach to childhood shaped the future conqueror. At a bustling food market, Michael samples the island’s wild herbs. He is captivated by the haunting harmonies of polyphonic singing, a sound deeply woven into the island’s soul. He then boards the legendary Trinichellu, Corsica’s historic metre-gauge mountain railway, for a breathtaking journey through the island’s rugged interior. In the heart of the wilderness, Michael discovers how cutting-edge technology and drones are being used in the battle against devastating wildfires, a crucial innovation protecting Corsica and beyond.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: In his first interview since resigning from government, former health secretary Wes Streeting talks about what went wrong for Keir Starmer, and why he should be the man to replace him.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an Impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out and they must try again tomorrow. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single Impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge in the tenth heat of the series. The specialist subjects are the life of Anne Lister, Dear Evan Hansen, Elizabeth I and the feature films of David Lynch.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Daisy mucks in with Tippy and Gus, getting her hands dirty, while Louis, seeking advice on the value of Oakley, visits Hilary and gets more insight than he bargained for. Daisy learns about the Behind the Vines showcase from Nic, and Vic delivers some bad news to Marissa and Don. Meanwhile, Daisy and Louis hope to ease their financial woes with a visit to the bank but discover they may not be on the same page after all and that failing to comply with the 'law of the land' can have consequences. Daisy makes the ultimate sacrifice for the future of Oakley, giving the run-down vineyard a chance of survival. Or will it merely be a stay of execution?

programme.title: Wonders of Life
programme.desc: Brian Cox considers what it is about our world that makes it a home for life and asks what transformed this once barren planet into the earth we know today.

programme.title: Flog It!

Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and Will Axon find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Christina is drawn to a 1950s toy pedal car, and Will finds a Mouseman tray. Paul Martin discovers how the Grand Union Canal was the waterway equivalent of the M1 as he takes to the water on a narrow boat and discovers what life was like for the boat people who ferried cargo from A to B.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Mediterranean railway adventure reaches its finale in Corsica as he boards one of Europe’s most dramatic railways, which winds through the island’s breathtaking landscapes. Braving the heights, he takes a close-up look at the Pont du Vecchio, a spectacular viaduct along the route. In a forest of ancient chestnut trees, Michael discovers how this humble fruit is turned into an unexpected foodstuff which has sustained Corsicans for centuries. Michael learns how a by-product from the hives of the aggressive Corsican black bee is being used to create a new wonder product. His journey culminates in the stunning mountain town of Corte, where he uncovers an astonishing piece of British history and comes face to face with the resilient spirit of the Corsican people.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin, along with guest judge and gardening fan Fred Sirieix, continue the search to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. First up is Anne’s Kilcootry Barn Gardens in Fintona, with two and a half acres of mixed gardens – filled with flower beds, a vegetable garden and an apple orchard. In Omagh, the judges visit a field of dreams – 17 acres of once-barren farmland that’s been transformed by Sir Bob and Lady Rosemary, with a formal Italianate area and a large woodland, planted with wildlife in mind. Finally, it’s off to the shores of Rossglass beach, overlooking Dundrum Bay, to visit artist Bernard’s romantic rose garden. Judges Diarmuid, Carol and Fred are searching for a garden which the owners have put their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide deserves to be the last contender for the title of Greatest Garden?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cuningham show how to help the pollinators in your garden and at Beechgrove as they focus on planting that will attract bees to your plot. Even if you don’t have a garden, Kirsty demonstrates how you can help the local ecosystem by sowing a meadow in a pot. She also discusses the best summer bulbs to plant now for fragrance and colour. Brian is back in the vegetable plot for his summer-long guide to productive gardening for beginners, and there is a demonstration of how to prune spring-flowering shrubs. All that and the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: It’s the end of the week at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show 2026, and Monty Don and Arit Anderson are celebrating the great British summer as we all get ready to spend more time in our gardens. Adam Frost has plenty of design ideas for garden structures, and Frances Tophill reveals which new variety has been named Plant of the Year.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Married at First Sight UK is one of Channel 4’s biggest shows, in which complete strangers marry in a mock-wedding and cameras follow what happens next. Panorama investigates allegations that raise serious concerns that welfare procedures on the reality show have failed contributors, leaving them at risk of harm. Noor Nanji speaks to three women who allege sexual misconduct by their former on-screen husbands. Two of the women say they were sexually assaulted. The men deny all the allegations against them, and both Channel 4 and CPL - the independent production company that makes the series - say the welfare protocols are robust and comprehensive. Following this Panorama investigation, Channel 4 has announced an external review into contributor welfare and has removed all previous seasons of MAFS UK.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through the islands of Sardinia and Corsica sees him leave Sardinia and arrive into Corsica, the most mountainous island in the Mediterranean. In Ajaccio, he delves into the early life of the island’s most famous son, Napoleon Bonaparte, discovering how Corsica’s unique approach to childhood shaped the future conqueror. At a bustling food market, Michael samples the island’s wild herbs. He is captivated by the haunting harmonies of polyphonic singing, a sound deeply woven into the island’s soul. He then boards the legendary Trinichellu, Corsica’s historic metre-gauge mountain railway, for a breathtaking journey through the island’s rugged interior. In the heart of the wilderness, Michael discovers how cutting-edge technology and drones are being used in the battle against devastating wildfires, a crucial innovation protecting Corsica and beyond.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an Impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out and they must try again tomorrow. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single Impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Planet Defenders
programme.desc: Megan is a wildlife expert who campaigns for animal rights and has a passion for shark conservation. Her mission is to look into the threats facing sharks in British waters and around the globe, from the deadly fin trade to industrial fishing, which have caused shark population numbers to fall dramatically in recent decades. One species she is keen to know more about is the blue shark, millions of which are caught each year for their fins, which can fetch thousands of dollars in Asia and have also ended up in Chinese restaurants in the UK. Megan also investigates the story behind a recent report that one of the nation’s favourite takeaways – fish and chips – has been linked to a species of shark which is listed as globally vulnerable and is on the brink of extinction in British waters. Megan meets up with marine biologists and shark conservationists to find out more about the dangers to British sharks and explores ways in which sharks and other fish species can be protected. As part of her mission, she heads to the Cornish coast and dons her snorkelling gear to try and get a glimpse of the beautiful blue shark in its natural habitat.

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: Twelve-year-old Laleeyah lives on the Crow Creek Native American reservation in South Dakota, USA. There aren’t many opportunities for people on the reservation, and life can be tough, but Laleeyah loves to learn about the traditions of her ancestors and takes pride in keeping them alive. Once a year there is the Pow Wow: a big, colourful, celebration where the whole Crow Creek tribe comes together to compete and celebrate with traditional dancing, music and dress. For several years running Laleeyah has been crowned Junior Miss Crow Creek - the best young dancer on the reservation. But since the last Pow Wow she has developed an illness called hyperthyroidism, which makes her feel weak and tired. As she comes to terms with her illness, Laleeyah still wants to hold on to the things she loves most: dancing, representing her tribe, and her crown. But will she have what it takes, and can she still be the dancing queen?

programme.title: Africa
programme.desc: Southern Africa is a riot of life and colour because of two great ocean currents that sweep around the continent's Cape. To the east, the warm Agulhas current, generating clouds that roll inland to the wettest place in southern Africa. To the west is the cold Benguela current, home to more great white sharks than anywhere else. Moisture-laden fog rolls inland, supporting wonderful desert garden. And where the two currents meet, the clash of warm and cold water creates one of the world's most fabulous natural spectacles: South Africa's sardine run. This is the greatest gathering of predators on the planet, including Africa's largest, the brydes whale.

programme.title: Planet Defenders
programme.desc: Megan is a wildlife expert who campaigns for animal rights and has a passion for shark conservation. Her mission is to look into the threats facing sharks in British waters and around the globe, from the deadly fin trade to industrial fishing, which have caused shark population numbers to fall dramatically in recent decades. One species she is keen to know more about is the blue shark, millions of which are caught each year for their fins, which can fetch thousands of dollars in Asia and have also ended up in Chinese restaurants in the UK. Megan also investigates the story behind a recent report that one of the nation’s favourite takeaways – fish and chips – has been linked to a species of shark which is listed as globally vulnerable and is on the brink of extinction in British waters. Megan meets up with marine biologists and shark conservationists to find out more about the dangers to British sharks and explores ways in which sharks and other fish species can be protected. As part of her mission, she heads to the Cornish coast and dons her snorkelling gear to try and get a glimpse of the beautiful blue shark in its natural habitat.

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: Twelve-year-old Laleeyah lives on the Crow Creek Native American reservation in South Dakota, USA. There aren’t many opportunities for people on the reservation, and life can be tough, but Laleeyah loves to learn about the traditions of her ancestors and takes pride in keeping them alive. Once a year there is the Pow Wow: a big, colourful, celebration where the whole Crow Creek tribe comes together to compete and celebrate with traditional dancing, music and dress. For several years running Laleeyah has been crowned Junior Miss Crow Creek - the best young dancer on the reservation. But since the last Pow Wow she has developed an illness called hyperthyroidism, which makes her feel weak and tired. As she comes to terms with her illness, Laleeyah still wants to hold on to the things she loves most: dancing, representing her tribe, and her crown. But will she have what it takes, and can she still be the dancing queen?

programme.desc: Southern Africa is a riot of life and colour because of two great ocean currents that sweep around the continent's Cape. To the east, the warm Agulhas current, generating clouds that roll inland to the wettest place in southern Africa. To the west is the cold Benguela current, home to more great white sharks than anywhere else. Moisture-laden fog rolls inland, supporting wonderful desert garden. And where the two currents meet, the clash of warm and cold water creates one of the world's most fabulous natural spectacles: South Africa's sardine run. This is the greatest gathering of predators on the planet, including Africa's largest, the brydes whale.

They reach their destination at the same time, and Otti and Roly finally get to sound the boat whistle. They are all directed towards a mysterious-looking cave where Chew Chew is waiting for both parcels. They deliver them at the same time, but they contain different things – one is full of biscuits and the other organic almond milk. They aren’t the same but they go really well together, just like the Squirrels and Hummingbirds!

Finally, a large cardboard tube provides inspiration for a terrific tube vulture.

They turn to Duggee for help, who uses his feeling cards to explain an array of feelings to Happy. All the Squirrels help by relaying their past experiences and the feelings that they evoked.

Not all his friends like the taste of dates at first, so let’s hope they enjoy them when the pie is ready. Sonny-Mac serves the pie to his friends at a special tea party, where everyone dresses very smartly.

We see how the parts are bent and moulded into different shapes to make the new parts of the trombone and Maddie uses a special gadget to measure the temperature and find out how the metals are heated and stuck together.

He’s a little shy, but eventually he comes out to meet them. Adorned with beautiful blue feathers and an impressive crest of feathers on his head, he’s truly a sight to see. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

The pair head to the local racetrack, where they go head-to-head in a sport known to the locals as 'the trots'. They end the day with a group of people who gather every week to immerse themselves in medieval fantasy role-play. The next day, Bradley and Barney hit the road and head to the city of Rockhampton, where they meet a man who went viral thanks to a very unexpected talent. Barney then has an adrenaline-fuelled treat in store for his dad as he's arranged for him to get behind the wheel of something slightly bigger than the RV… a monster.

programme.title: Grantchester

He has lined up a programme of celebrations for Easter and the whole village has embraced it - well, most of them, as local Reg sits outside the church protesting with his homemade placard that Christianity is getting too commercialised. Tragedy strikes, however, when a gunshot is heard and Reg is found dead, seemingly having taken his own life - Geordie, though suspects foul play as Reg was seen arguing with his fiance shortly before and something doesn't quite add up about this decorated war hero. Meanwhile, Alphy is getting a reputation for dating most of the girls in the village, love is clearly in the air as Geordie seems to be constantly walking in on Larry and Miss Scott canoodling around the station, Cathy is facing a danger to the workforce at Swinnerton's, and Leonard worries that Daniel will reconcile with his parents.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. The death of a student plunges Geordie and Alphy into a world of academic adversaries where two research groups are racing to prove and publish their newest theses before the other - prestige, fame and a place in the history books are all at stake. With claims of plagiarism, favouritism and cheating being thrown around, it's clear some of these learned fellows can be more immature than the students... across the case, one of the professors is an Indian woman confounded by Alphy, someone who seems to have so little interest in his own heritage and has made himself into an image of quintessential white Britishness. While Alphy, who is normally so cool and self-assured, is a little unnerved by her, he feels surer of himself with Meg until it is revealed that her father is the bishop who tried to have him replaced - elsewhere, Leonard struggles with his father's death in Daniel's absence, and Geordie makes more of an effort to listen to Cathy as her work input is overlooked.

programme.title: Scott & Bailey
programme.desc: Drama series following two Manchester police officers. In the first of a two-part story, DCI Gill Murray, DC Janet Scott, DC Rachel Bailey and the team are called in when a badly burned body turns up in remote woodland and is followed a few days later by another. Working alongside the formidable DCI Julie Dodson, the officers realise that the victims were tortured before they were killed. They make an arrest, but when the brother of prime suspect Nadia Hicks is brutally murdered, it becomes clear that their investigation has only scratched the surface. Meanwhile, Rachel's estranged brother Dom arrives on her doorstep, and she does not have the heart to turn him away. Janet also has a guest - her mother Dorothy. Unfortunately, Dorothy winds up Janet's husband Adrian, and it is not long before he packs his bags. At work, Kevin leaps to Rachel's defence when a murder suspect turns violent, but his thunder is stolen by sexy traffic cop Sean.

programme.title: Scott & Bailey
programme.desc: Second of a two-part story. The team finally break down the wall of silence maintained by their four murder suspects and uncover the shockingly banal truth behind the killings. Meanwhile, Rachel cannot fight her attraction to Sean, but will she regret her actions? At the same time, Janet tries to keep her private life secret, but Taisie spills the beans to Andy at Rachel's birthday celebrations.

Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.
